prompt:

Behind her, a richly painted background with layered painterly colour, subtle visible brushwork, atmospheric perspective and cinematic depth. Luminous, rich colours; crisp focal details on the face and costume, softer painted edges toward the distance. No flat single-tone cel shading, photographic appearance, semi-realistic face or plastic 3D-render finish. Outfit: an ice cutter look fitted to her body — a cropped fur-trimmed jerkin over a short wool top, short wool breeches, thick wool socks and fur boots, showing her shoulders, collarbones and legs as far as the outfit allows, following her curvy figure — a slim waist and rounded hips; intimate areas covered.
POSTURE: kneeling on one knee, the other foot planted flat in front of her.

LEFT HAND: her own left hand is planted on the ground beside her.
PROP: with her own right hand she holds a long ice saw at chest height; it is all she holds.

EXPRESSION: brows level, eyes bright and steady, closed-lip smile with a firm mouth.
Scene note: she is the ice cutter kneeling on the frozen lake to split a clear block of ice cleanly in two

Leave behind everything she wears in the attached image — no crown, tiara, helmet, feathers, headpiece, hairpins from it, armour or regalia; her hair is styled for the everyday outfit, with at most one small accessory.

Her element — meitnerium: a heavy synthetic metal below iridium, first made in 1982 in a research city as a single atom, and the only element named for one real woman alone: an exiled physicist who, on a snowy winter walk in a forest, sat on a fallen tree trunk and worked out on scraps of paper that a heavy nucleus can stretch like a trembling drop of liquid and split cleanly in two, releasing great energy; the prize for that discovery went to her colleague alone, and she refused all work on the weapon it made possible — may show in the outfit's details, motifs or small accessories.

Light: the place's own light, lit and coloured the way this style renders light and skin.
